newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Direct Capital has 10 pct of Palliser Wines.
newsitem.headline: Direct Capital has 10 pct of Palliser Wines.

text.p: New Zealand investment company Direct Capital Partners has taken a 10 percent stake in Martinborough winemaker Palliser Estate Wines, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Tuesday.
Spokesman Mark Hutton said Direct Capital had acquired the holding through a private share placement and through trading of the unlisted company's shares on secondary markets.
"Palliser Estate is a top-class, profitable operation which is now looking to expand further," Hutton said.
Direct Capital specialises in investment in small growing businesses.
No price was disclosed for the purchase.
Palliser Estate Wines was formed in 1984 through the merger of two vineyards and the construction of a winery.
Exports grew by 41 percent last year and the company recently bought the Pinnacles vineyard north of Martinborough to meet that growing demand.
Hutton said the Palliser acquisition complemented the company's 49 percent stake in Nobilo Vintners.
"Both companies are focused on export sales, have won significant orders from international airlines and developed new markets, such as Asia," he said.
Hutton said the company would continue to seek opportunities to invest in the wine industry, and would possibly take a stake in other selected unlisted companies trading on the secondary market.
